name: Push Poker
description: Push is a five-card stud poker variant in which players may pay an agreed price to reject an upcard offered by the dealer and receive the next card from the deck instead. Four rounds of card-offer and pushing are followed by betting; highest hand wins.

overview.description: Push is a five-card stud poker variant in which players may pay an agreed price to reject an upcard offered by the dealer and receive the next card from the deck instead. Four rounds of card-offer and pushing are followed by betting; highest hand wins.

history.origins: Push is a five-card stud variant in the Pass the Trash family; players may pay to reject an offered upcard and receive the next card from the deck.
timeline: 20th century: Stud variant in the Pass the Trash family with paid push option for offered upcards.
history.evolution: Adds a paid rejection (push) option to standard stud card distribution.

setup.dealing: One hole card face down to each player. Then the dealer offers one card face up to the player to his left; that player may accept it or pay the agreed price to push it and receive the next card from the deck (second card must be accepted). The next player is offered the pushed card or a new card; this continues for all players. After each of four such rounds there is a betting round. Final hand is five cards (one hole, four up); highest hand wins.
setup.equipment: Standard deck and chips. Push price (e.g. 5 times minimum bet) agreed in advance.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest five-card poker hand at showdown.
rules.gameplay: After one hole card each, the dealer offers one card face up to the player to his left. That player may accept it or pay the agreed price to push it and receive the next card from the deck (must accept the second). The next player is offered the pushed card if the previous player pushed, otherwise a new card; same accept-or-push choice. This continues until all have received a card; any card pushed by the last player is discarded. Betting round begins with the player showing the highest hand. Three more rounds of offering and pushing (each starting with a fresh card to the first active player to dealer's left), each followed by a betting round. After the fourth round all active players have five cards (four face up). Showdown: highest hand wins.
keyRules: Push price (e.g. 5× minimum bet) must be agreed before play.
Second card when pushing must be accepted.
First card offered in each new round is always a fresh card from the deck to the first active player to dealer's left.
Betting rounds are begun by the player with the highest hand showing.

strategy.basic: Push only when the offered card is weak and the cost is worth the chance of a better card; otherwise accept and save chips for betting.
strategy.intermediate: Track which upcards opponents have; push more often when you need to avoid pairing low or when the next card could complete a draw.
strategy.advanced: Balance push cost against pot odds; use position to push selectively so the next player gets a card you know is bad for their board.
tips: Agree push price before the hand (e.g. 5× minimum bet).
If the last player pushes, that card is discarded face down.

variations.name: Roll your own
variations.description: All cards dealt face down; pushing is free. After four rounds each player has one hole card and four face-up cards; can be played all-high, all-low, or high-low with declaration.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses same engine constants; no overrides needed.

variations.name: Substitution
variations.description: After the final betting round, active players may pay an agreed price (e.g. 10× minimum bet) to discard one card and receive a replacement from the deck; then a final betting round and showdown.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds substitution phase; no engine constant overrides documented.

scoring.description: Pot is won by the highest five-card poker hand at showdown, or by the last player remaining after all others fold.
scoring.winCondition: Highest five-card hand at showdown wins the pot; standard poker hand ranking.
